text:
Mishra: seeing a flurry of capacity signals from asia-east1 this morning, GPUs going into 'unstable' and a subset getting drained. latency for short-chat tier jumping to 600-900ms and a handful of 503s. rolling alerts from the LB.
Sam: yup saw it too, started routing ~20% of traffic to dedicated pools as a quick mitigation. watch for increased token spend.
autoscaler-bot: [1805236820] scaling event: pool=mixed-gpu-asia, action=scale-down, reason=provider_capacity_signal, instances_affected=18
Leah: can we flip a routing override to prefer warm dedicated? quick command available?
Henry: I pushed a temporary override to prefer-dedicated for chat-small: `curl -X POST https://internal.redwood/api/v1/route-override -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' -d '{"policy":"prefer-dedicated","ttl_s":900}'` — takes effect now.
Mishra: confirmed traffic shift. error rate down, p95 latency from 820ms -> 210ms after the shift. thanks.
Sam: we still need a durable plan: mixed pools are cheaper but these transient provider signals are spiky. propose: 1) increase minimum on-demand buffer in asia-east1 from 10% -> 25% for business hours; 2) enable aggressive KV prefix caching for small-chat; 3) fallback model variant w/ fewer layers if scaled-out capacity drops.
Leah: agree on buffer. can we do a staged switch to avoid big cost shock? e.g. ramp 10% -> 25% over 30m if signal persists.
Henry: put a quick automation: if provider_capacity_signal count > 5 in 10m then start ramp to 25% over 15m, revert after 60m no-signal. I can add the policy in the autoscaler.
CostOps: FYI that ramp is expected to add ~18-24% infra spend for the region while active. approve?
Mishra: approve for today as incident mitigation. track cost and add an incident tag so finance review sees it.
Sam: also adding a canary route to us-central with warm standby images — will shift stateless chat only, not llm weights. reducing cross-region egress.
Leah: quick log snippet from one affected node: ```
[2026-09-09T18:07:23Z] preempt-signal received: reason=capacity-throttle, provider=cloudX, grace_s=30
[2026-09-09T18:07:55Z] kvcache-evict: prefix=conv-*, entries=34
[2026-09-09T18:08:02Z] connection-reset: peer=10.20.8.101, code=ECONNRESET
```
Mishra: good capture. please add those lines to the postmortem.
Henry: autoscaler rule pushed: `rule id=cap-surge-asia-2026-09-09`, action=ramp-on-demand, params={"min_buffer_pct":25,"ramp_window_s":900,"cooldown_s":3600}. monitoring alerts will fire when active.
autoscaler-bot: [1805237005] rule_applied: cap-surge-asia-2026-09-09 -> active
Sam: next steps: 1) postmortem template (I'll start), 2) cost tag applied (Leah), 3) eval whether model-quant vs on-demand buffer gives better cost/latency tradeoff.
CostOps: noted cost tag and will flag for monthly review.
Mishra: thanks all — keep updates here. if we see signal repeat tonight we'll move to 50% buffer and a pre-approved spend cap.
Leah: ack, monitoring dashboards updated and alert thresholds lowered for p95. :eyes:
Sam: closing for now, keeping thread pinned. :thumbsup:
